Autoimmune Hepatitis Mouse Model Liver Immune Cell Atlas

Single-cell transcriptomic and TCR resource for a spontaneous mouse model of autoimmune hepatitis.

Study overview

Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is characterized by persistent sterile hepatic inflammation and progressive fibrosis, yet treatment relies on broad immunosuppression. The cellular mechanisms sustaining pathogenic autoreactive T-cell responses in the liver remain poorly defined, partly because few experimental models reproduce spontaneous disease progression. In this study, we introduced mice deficient in DNase II and the type I interferon receptor (Dnase2a−/− Ifnar1−/−) as a spontaneous model of type 1 autoimmune hepatitis recapitulating key features of human disease, including interface hepatitis, elevated ALT, progressive fibrosis, antinuclear antibodies, and hypergammaglobulinemia. Paired single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor sequencing were used to characterize the liver immune-cell landscape and connect T-cell transcriptional states with clonotype expansion.

    Method

    Single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing

    CD3+ fractions from livers of Het and DKO mice were sorted for paired scRNA/TCR-seq. CD3− fractions from livers of 2 Het and 2 DKO mice were pooled within genotype for scRNA-seq. Libraries were generated as previously described.90 Approximately 20,000 cells per sample were loaded onto a 10x Chromium Chip G and 5′ gene expression libraries were prepared with the Chromium Single-Cell 5′ Library and Gel Bead Kit (10x Genomics) according to the manufacturer's instructions. T cell receptor libraries were prepared from the CD3+ samples with the mouse T cell Single Cell V(D)J Enrichment Kit (10x Genomics). Library quality was assessed using a TapeStation (Agilent), and libraries were sequenced by NovaSeq6000 (Illumina) to obtain a minimum of 20,000 paired-end reads per cell. Single-cell TCR libraries were multiplexed and sequenced by NovaSeq6000 (Illumina) to obtain a minimum of 5,000 paired-end reads per cell. The sequencing specifications were set according to the manufacturer’s specification (10x Genomics).

    Biological question

    How does chronic innate immune activation reshape the liver immune compartment and sustain pathogenic T-cell responses?

    The atlas is designed as an extension of the manuscript: readers can move beyond the figures, search their own genes of interest, compare conditions, and locate expanded T-cell clonotypes within the total T-cell and activated-CD8 landscapes.
